name: Yachats
note: Yachats, Oregon, from OpenStreetMap on its real ground: the village on its terrace where the Yachats River meets the Pacific, the 804 Trail along the basalt, and Cape Perpetua to the south, its stone shelter 230 m over Devil's Churn, Thor's Well and the Spouting Horn.
attribution: Map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (lidar).

fetch._: from the Geofabrik Oregon extract (tools/pbf-to-overpass.py); every building is kept in the village and on the cape

cutWater._: lidar records the river surface a metre or two over the sea: the river and the ponds are cut under the water level

coast._: the coastline decides what is sea; the USGS survey reads its sea as the surface, so only what it puts at the water is sunk (tools/build-osm-city.py coast_cut)

terrain._: the terrace, the river's valley and Cape Perpetua's headland; the open sea is the datum (tools/build-osm-city.py)

_sky: the Oregon coast's sky: pale at the horizon with the marine haze, the sun going down into the sea

defaultHeights._: the village: houses of a storey and a half under steep gables, motels and inns of two and three

facadeStyles._: cedar shakes: most gone silver in the salt air, some kept brown with oil
painted siding in the greys, sage, slate and sand the coast wears

palette._: cedar, weathered shingle and grey paint

pitchAll._: every roof pitched, for the rain

_treeSpecies: the Oregon coast: Sitka spruce in the fog belt, shore pine twisted by the wind over the beaches, hemlock in the forest, red alder along the creeks, and rhododendrons in every yard

dress._: src/core/dress.js: wood decks with a little roof on some of the houses (not Portland's craftsman porches); awnings on the shops along the highway

vehicles._: src/core/traffic.js: the 101 and its log trucks and campers; Lincoln County Transit's coast bus

crowds._: [lat, lon, radius, people]: the state recreation area, Thor's Well, Devil's Churn, the visitor center, the West Shelter, Smelt Sands, the village

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: West Shelter
landmarks.info: Built of the cape's own basalt by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933, 230 m over the sea at the top of Cape Perpetua. On a clear day you see seventy miles of coast and thirty-seven miles out to sea; in the war it was a lookout for submarines.

landmarks.name: Cape Perpetua Visitor Center
landmarks.info: The Forest Service's center under the cape, its glass looking west down to the rocks: the trails start here, down to the tide pools and the Spouting Horn, and up to the Giant Spruce and the stone shelter.

landmarks.name: Little Log Church & Museum
landmarks.info: Built of logs by the village in 1927, the Little Log Church is now its museum and its wedding chapel: a steep roof, a small belfry, a view of the sea from the pews.

landmarks.name: Cleft of the Rock Light
landmarks.info: A private lighthouse on the north flank of Cape Perpetua, built in 1976 by the lighthouse historian Jim Gibbs to the pattern of Fiddle Reef's in British Columbia; its light is on the charts.

landmarks.name: Thor's Well
landmarks.info: A hole in the basalt shelf, the roof of a sea cave fallen in: at high tide the sea fills it from below, spouts out of it, and then drains back in as if the ocean were going down a plughole. Watched from the shelf, at a distance: sneaker waves are how people die here.

landmarks.name: Spouting Horn
landmarks.info: At the head of Cook's Chasm, a crack in the roof of a sea cave: when a wave fills the cave, the air and the sea come out of the top of it in a jet.

landmarks.name: Devil's Churn
landmarks.info: An inlet cut into the basalt along a fault, narrowing to a slot a few metres wide: the waves come up it, slam into the end and throw spray higher than the trail. The Trail of Restless Waters goes down to it.

landmarks.name: Yachats River Bridge
landmarks.info: The Oregon Coast Highway crosses the Yachats River at the head of its little estuary on a three-span concrete girder bridge of 1977, 223 feet long, where the smelt and the salmon come in. Yachats is said to come from the Siletz for the dark water at the foot of the mountain.

landmarks.name: Cook's Chasm Bridge
landmarks.info: The highway crosses the head of Cook's Chasm on a bridge of 2003, 159 feet long; under it the Spouting Horn goes off with the incoming waves.

landmarks.name: Cummins Creek Bridge
landmarks.info: One of Conde McCullough's coast bridges, 1931: a concrete deck girder 185 feet long over Cummins Creek, with his balustrade of round-arched openings and a pylon at each corner. The creek comes down out of the Cummins Creek Wilderness, one of the last old-growth Sitka spruce valleys on the coast.

yachats._: src/yachats/coast.js: the forest grown over the land; the surf; the basalt

treeDense._: no engine woodland: the forest is coast.js's, grown round the camera, and the reserves here are mostly sea

bridgeHeights._: the trails' footbridges sit on their ground; the highway's decks over the water are level with the banks (bridgeDeck)
